column1: # THE ERROR-CODE REGISTRY -- the shared contract for engine error codes.
# Every error code either implementation can attach to a failure is
# registered here with its CLASS. This file is the source of truth: both
# runners (ts/test/spec.test.ts, go/spec_test.go) execute each row below
# (mode `errcode`) against the engine's own code->class table
# runner additionally asserts SET EQUALITY between this file and its
# engine table -- a code present in an engine but absent here (or the
# reverse) fails the suite in that engine.
#   code  : the frozen snake_case code string (the NilVal `why`).
#           Codes are a CONTRACT: append-only, renames forbidden. A code
#           that ends in `:` or `[` is a dynamic-prefix family -- the
#           and class lookup falls back to the longest registered prefix.
#   class : one of conflict | incomplete | reference | parse | budget |
#           internal (see below). Classes drive report verdicts and exit
#           class change is a breaking change.
#   since : the version line (TypeScript series) at which the code was
#           first REGISTERED. Codes predating the registry all carry the
#   conflict   : the source asks for something that can never hold --
#                two values with no common lower bound, a value refused
#                by a language rule, an impossible function argument.
#   incomplete : nothing contradicts, but residue remains -- a value the
#                truth requires has not been supplied yet.
#   reference  : a name or path that does not resolve.
#   parse      : the source text itself is malformed or unusable.
#   budget     : an evaluation bound was exceeded (cycles, passes,
#   internal   : the engine reached a state it should not reach.
# RULINGS the class column encodes (decided at registry inception):
#   - decimal_budget is class CONFLICT, not budget: the exactness budget
#     is a fixed language rule about the VALUE (4096 digits / scale
#     4096), not an evaluation resource -- no re-run with a larger
#     budget exists, so the repair action is "change the value", which
#     is what conflict means. The budget class is reserved for
#   - lossy_integer_literal is class CONFLICT for the same reason: the
#     literal is well-formed but refused by a value rule; the repair is
#   - unknown_function is class REFERENCE: a name that fails to resolve,
#     exactly like an unresolved path or variable.
#     it never surfaces to user-visible output, and the engines assert
#     set equality, so registering it would claim otherwise.
# parse -- the source text is malformed or unusable
# conflict -- no common lower bound, or a value refused by a rule
# incomplete -- residue: the truth requires more than was supplied
# reference -- a name or path that does not resolve
# budget -- an evaluation bound was exceeded
# internal -- the engine reached a state it should not reach
